memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "For whoever wants to save their life will lose it, but whoever loses their life for me will find it." — Matthew 16:25

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
In many popular card games, the goal is counter-intuitive: to win, you must be the first to have nothing left in your hand. You "lose" your cards to "gain" the victory. There is a profound spiritual coincidence in this. The world teaches us to hoard to gather as many "cards" (possessions, titles, and pride) as possible. But the Kingdom of God operates on the principle of the "Brilliant Give-Away."
To "lose our possessions cleverly" means to invest them where they truly count. When we give away our time, our resources, and our very selves for the sake of the Gospel, we aren't just losing; we are strategically discarding the temporary to make room for the eternal. Just as a clever player knows when to drop a "Wild" card or a "Skip," the wise believer knows that letting go of earthly attachments is the fastest way to reach the "Mark." We empty our hands of the world so that God can fill them with the Eternal Reward. Winning isn't about what you keep; it’s about how brilliantly you gave it all away for His sake.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "He is no fool who gives what he cannot keep to gain what he cannot lose." — Jim Elliot

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, help me to play the game of life with spiritual brilliance. Teach me the art of the divine discard to let go of my pride, my greed, and my earthly security. May I be clever in my stewardship and passionate in my giving, keeping my eyes fixed on the mark of the high calling in Christ Jesus. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Don't be afraid when you feel you are losing things of this world. If you are losing them for Christ, you are actually moving closer to the final shout of victory. Give away with joy today!
